name: mcp__local-fs__edit_file
description: Make a TARGETED change to an existing file via search-and-replace (oldString → newString), without needing to know or send the whole file's content. This is the PREFERRED way to change an existing file — use this instead of write_file when you're only adding/changing/removing a bounded part (e.g. adding an import, changing a function's body, adding a new export). oldString must match exactly once in the file (unless replaceAll:true is used) — this is a safety guard so an edit never hits the wrong place or accidentally overwrites something you haven't seen. If you're unsure of the exact current text: read the file (or the relevant symbol/section) with read_file first.

newString.description: The text to replace oldString with.

oldString.description: The exact text string to replace (incl. whitespace/indentation). Must match EXACTLY once in the file, otherwise the edit is rejected (see replaceAll for multiple occurrences).

path.description: Path to the file to edit, relative to the sandbox root. The file must already exist.

replaceAll.description: If true: replace ALL occurrences of oldString instead of requiring exactly one match. Use with caution — default false requires exactly one match to avoid unintended changes.

name: mcp__local-fs__file_stat
description: Get metadata (size, type, last modified) for a file or directory. Read-only.

path.description: Path to get metadata for, relative to the sandbox root.

name: mcp__local-fs__find_files
description: Find files based on FILE NAME/PATH (not content) within the sandbox, using ripgrep --files. Read-only. Use this when you know (or are guessing) a file's name but not where it lives — e.g. find_files({ pattern: '*invite*' }) to find all files with 'invite' in the name. Complements search_files (which searches file CONTENT) and list_dir (which requires you to already be in the right directory).

path.description: Directory to search within, relative to the sandbox root.

pattern.description: Glob pattern or substring to match against FILE NAME/PATH (not content), e.g. '*.ts', '*invite*', 'src/**/*.test.ts'. If the pattern doesn't contain any of the characters * ? [ ] it's treated as a substring match against the full relative path.

name: mcp__local-fs__list_dir
description: List files and directories within the sandbox. Read-only. Use this to explore the project structure.

path.description: Directory to list, relative to the sandbox root. Default '.'

name: mcp__local-fs__read_file
description: Read the content of a text file within the sandbox. Read-only. This is the primary way for the agent to get context. Default (no 'full' or 'symbol' given): returns a compact OUTLINE instead of the whole file: for .md all headings/subheadings with line numbers, for .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx all top-level const/function/interface/type/class/enum signatures without body, for .json/.yaml/.yml all key paths recursively (e.g. foo.bar.baz, foo.bar, foo). Other file types are returned in full as usual. Pass 'symbol' to fetch a specific part (heading section/function/key value), or 'full: true' for the entire file.

full.description: Get the entire file content as-is, without outline shortening. USE SPARINGLY: read without 'full' first (you get an outline), then fetch specific parts with 'symbol'. For files larger than ~4KB of an outlineable type (.md/.ts/.json/.yaml), 'reason' is also required together with full:true.

path.description: Path to the file, relative to the sandbox root.

reason.description: Only required if full:true is used on a file >4KB of an outlineable type: a short justification for why you need the entire file content instead of outline/symbol (e.g. 'need to see the whole file context for a large refactor').

symbol.description: Fetch just a specific part of the file instead of the whole outline: for .md a heading section (matched against heading text, substring/case-insensitive), for .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx a symbol name (function/const/interface/type/class/enum, full source code incl. body; for imports you can match on the module path, a substring of it, or an imported name, e.g. 'create' or 'member.create'), for .json/.yaml/.yml a key path (e.g. 'foo.bar.baz' or 'items[0].name').

name: mcp__local-fs__search_files
description: Search for text or regex in file CONTENT within the sandbox, using ripgrep. Read-only. Good for finding where something is defined or used. NOTE: this searches file content, not file names — if you're looking for a file based on its name/path (e.g. 'where is invite-member-command.ts?'), use find_files instead.

filePattern.description: Optional glob filter for file names, e.g. '*.ts' or '*.md' (ripgrep --glob).

path.description: Directory (or file) to search within, relative to the sandbox root.

query.description: Text string or regex to search for in file content.

regex.description: Interpret query as regex instead of plain text (default: plain text search).

name: mcp__local-fs__web_fetch
description: Fetch a single URL over http(s). Read-only, GET only (no cookies/auth/state). HTML pages are converted to markdown-ish readable text (headings, links as [text](url)), and by default only an OUTLINE is returned (page title + all headings with their nesting, like read_file does for local .md files) instead of the full page — this avoids flooding context with a huge page. See 'Efficient usage' below for how 'section', 'full', and 'raw' fit together. Single-page apps (React/Vue/Angular etc.) that render content with client-side JavaScript are handled automatically: by default ('render: "auto"') a plain static fetch is tried first, and if the result looks like an empty, unrendered SPA shell, a headless Chromium browser (via playwright-core) renders the page and the real, post-JavaScript content is returned instead. Use 'render: "always"' to force a browser render, or 'render: "never"' to disable it. Rendering is slower (headless browser) so 'auto' only pays that cost when it looks necessary. Requests to localhost/private/link-local addresses are blocked. Responses are capped in size (~1000000 bytes fetched, ~50000 chars returned) and time out after 15000ms. Efficient usage, in order: (1) web_fetch({url}) first, to see the outline (headings only) without spending context on the full page; (2) web_fetch({url, section: "..."}) to read the one or two sections that look relevant, in markdown; (3) only if you specifically need exact, unconverted markup (e.g. a table's real structure, tab/accordion boundaries, an element's attributes, or markdown conversion looks like it dropped/garbled something) add 'raw: true' — optionally still combined with 'section' to keep it scoped to one part instead of the whole raw page. Avoid reaching for 'raw: true' or 'full: true' by default: they cost more context and, for 'raw', lose the readable formatting most tasks don't need.

full.description: If true, skip outline mode and return the full converted page content (still capped by the overall size limit). Ignored when 'raw' is true (raw mode never does markdown conversion, so there's no outline to skip). Default false.

raw.description: Last resort, not a starting point: fetch the outline and/or a 'section' in markdown first, and only set 'raw: true' if that's not enough (e.g. you need a table's real structure, tab/accordion boundaries, an element's exact attributes, a JSON/plain-text API body, or the markdown conversion looks wrong). When true, returns the response body as-is instead of converting HTML to markdown, and takes precedence over 'full' and 'render' (no markdown conversion, no SPA rendering happen in raw mode). Combine with 'section' to scope raw mode to one part of an HTML page instead of dumping the whole raw document: it matches an <h1>-<h6> tag by its visible text (substring, case-insensitive) and returns the raw HTML from that heading through the next heading of equal-or-higher level. Default false.

render.description: Controls headless-browser (JavaScript) rendering for single-page apps: 'auto' (default) fetches statically first and only falls back to rendering with a headless browser if the page looks like an unrendered SPA shell (e.g. an empty #root/#app div); 'always' forces a browser render even if the static fetch looked fine (slower, but authoritative for pages with optimistic heuristics); 'never' disables rendering entirely, even for obvious SPA shells.

section.description: Fetch just one section of the page instead of the whole thing: matched against a heading's text (substring, case-insensitive), returning that heading through the next heading of equal-or-higher level. Use this after seeing the outline (call web_fetch({url}) first), similar to read_file's 'symbol' parameter. Works whether or not 'raw' is also set: without 'raw' you get that section in markdown (the normal, cheaper choice); with 'raw: true' you get that section's exact unconverted HTML instead of the whole raw page.

url.description: The absolute http(s) URL to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/page'.

name: mcp__local-fs__web_search
description: Search the web for a query and return a list of results (title, URL, snippet). Read-only. Backed by DuckDuckGo's HTML results page, so no API key is required. Use web_fetch afterwards to read the full content of a specific result URL.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-20, default 8).

name: mcp__local-fs__write_file
description: Write (create or overwrite) a file within the sandbox with the ENTIRE file content at once. WARNING: this replaces the full content of the file — if you only want to change part of an existing file (e.g. a function, a line, adding an import), use edit_file instead, which makes a targeted change without you needing to know or send the whole file's content. Use write_file to CREATE a new file, or when you deliberately want to replace a file's full content and you have actually read the whole file (full:true) first.

content.description: The complete file content to write (replaces any existing content).

createDirs.description: Create missing directories in the path if they don't exist.

path.description: Path to the file to write, relative to the sandbox root.
